data.title: shadcn/ui
data.tagline: A collection of editable UI component code that you add to a React project
data.learningOutcome: You can tell that a shadcn/ui Button lives in the project and must be maintained there.
data.description: Adding Button puts component files in your project, so changing those files changes the buttons on your site. It is not an online component service; your project owns the maintenance after you add it.

learning.assumes: You know a project contains files and includes buttons.
learning.outcome: You can tell that a shadcn/ui Button lives in the project and must be maintained there.

explanation.title: The command adds files
explanation.text: Adding Button writes component files into the current project.

explanation.title: The files are yours to change
explanation.text: Open the Button file to change its style, size, or behavior.

explanation.title: The preview uses that code
explanation.text: After you save, the page uses the updated project component.

data.boundary: Before adding a component, check whether the project already has one. Afterward, it is not an untouched external black box: review upgrades and changes in your files.

lessonPractice.title: After running the shadcn/ui command to add Button, how should the team understand the component?

options.label: Button code now lives in the project, pages import that file, and the project owns future changes and upgrades
options.feedback: Correct. shadcn/ui provides component source that enters the project, not a remote black-box service.

options.label: Button remains hosted by shadcn/ui, so the project can only change call parameters and cannot edit the component file
options.feedback: The add command writes code into the project, where it can be edited and must be maintained.

options.label: Button automatically follows every upstream update without reviewing local changes or compatibility
options.feedback: A local component does not upgrade safely by itself; updates still require review of project changes and usage.

data.agentPrompt: First check whether this project has initialized shadcn/ui and already contains a Button component. Reuse an existing Button instead of generating a duplicate. If shadcn/ui is initialized but Button is missing, run `npx shadcn@latest add button` from the project root, then use the generated Button on an existing page. Tell me where the component file was written, run the project checks, and open the page to verify its appearance and click behavior.
